means.en: Deciding how much to spend, how much to save, where to invest, and how to prepare for future needs.
Money a person receives, regularly or now and then, for work done or goods sold. Salary, business profit, rent, interest and dividends are all income.
A fixed amount an employer pays a worker, usually every month.
A plan of the money coming in and how it will be spent and saved over a period.
An amount you want to have by a date, such as a bicycle in six months.
Keeping a part of your income for later use. Savings build up over time.
A clay or tin pot with a slot for coins, broken or opened to count the savings.
A rise in the prices of goods and services over time.
How much a sum of money can buy. It falls when prices rise and the money does not grow.
Putting savings into assets such as a bank deposit, gold or shares, to protect their value and earn a return.
Something you own that has value, such as money in a bank, gold, land or shares.

plain.en: how fast it turns into cash

means.en: How easily something can be turned into cash when needed, without losing value. Cash is the most liquid.

plain.en: payment for the use of money

means.en: Money a bank or borrower pays for the use of your money, or that you pay when you borrow.
Interest left in the account earns interest of its own, so the money grows faster each year.
The amount first deposited or borrowed, before any interest.

plain.en: money left in a bank for a fixed time

means.en: A lump sum kept with a bank or post office for a fixed period at a rate fixed on the first day.
A whole amount of money paid or deposited at one time.

plain.en: the time until the money comes back

means.en: The time from the day money is put in to the day it is paid back.
A way to lend money to a government or a company for a fixed period. The borrower pays interest and returns the money on the maturity date.
A bond issued by a company to raise money. It usually pays more than a government bond because it carries more risk.

plain.en: a small part of a company

means.en: A small part of the ownership of a company. Its price goes up and down.
A part of a company's profit paid to the people who own its shares.

plain.en: a number for the share market

means.en: An index of the Bombay Stock Exchange that follows 30 large companies from different parts of the economy.
A pool of money from many investors, invested by a professional fund manager in shares, bonds or other assets.

plain.en: the person who invests the pool

means.en: A professional who decides where a mutual fund's money is invested.
Putting money in many different investments, so one fall cannot sink it all.
The chance of losing money.
The length of time money can stay invested before you need it.

plain.en: paying a little to cover a big loss

means.en: A legal contract: you pay a regular premium to an insurance company, and it pays for the losses your policy covers.
The regular amount paid to an insurance company for cover.
A request to the insurance company to pay for a loss the policy covers.
Many people pay into a common pool, and those who meet a loss are paid from it.
Money borrowed now and paid back later, usually with interest.
Money owed to somebody.
A fixed amount paid every month to repay a loan. Each EMI includes part of the principal and the interest.

plain.en: a compulsory payment to the government

means.en: A compulsory payment by people and businesses to the government, to pay for public services.
A direct tax paid on the income a person earns in a financial year.
A tax paid directly on a person's income or a business's profit.
A tax added to the price of goods and services, such as GST.
Goods and Services Tax: an indirect tax added to the price of goods and services.

plain.en: an amount taken off before tax

means.en: A fixed amount salaried people and pensioners subtract from their income before tax is worked out.

plain.en: the income the tax is worked on

means.en: Income left after deductions. The tax slabs are applied to this amount.

plain.en: an income range with one rate

means.en: A range of taxable income taxed at one rate. Each part of the income is taxed at its own slab's rate.

plain.en: higher incomes pay a higher rate

means.en: A system where tax rises with income, so people with more can give a larger share.
A yearly statement of how much a person earned and how much tax is due.
The year used for tax: 1 April to 31 March.
Covers medical costs such as hospital stays, medicines, tests and treatment.
Pays the family if the person who earns for it dies, to meet daily expenses, schooling and loans.
Covers vehicles, homes, businesses, crops, animals and other property.
A bond issued by the government. It is generally safer than a company bond and pays a steadier, lower rate.

plain.en: a bank account for keeping money

means.en: A bank account where money stays safe, earns a small interest, and can be taken out on any day.
A savings scheme backed by the government. Money is put in for 15 years and earns a fixed rate of interest.
A savings certificate sold at post offices. The money stays for five years and earns a fixed rate of interest.

plain.en: a government savings scheme for a girl child

means.en: A savings scheme backed by the government in which parents save for a daughter's education or marriage, at a fixed rate of interest.

plain.en: what the insurance will pay for

means.en: The losses an insurance policy promises to pay for, up to a set amount, while the premium is paid.

plain.en: a loan to pay for studies

means.en: A loan taken to pay for a course. It is paid back later, often from the higher income the course helps the student earn.
